name: Brevo
summary: Email, SMS and a light CRM, priced by monthly send volume rather than contact count — cheaper for a large list you email selectively. Model your real send volume if you mail frequently.
best_for: businesses with large contact lists who email selectively and want to pay by send volume, not list size
skip_if: you email your whole list daily — the per-send model can flip from cheap to costly at high frequency
honest_knock: Charging by sends looks cheaper for a big list you email rarely, but the send tiers cap stored contacts too: 5,000 sends a month stores only 500 contacts, and a 20,000-contact list needs the 20,000-send tier whatever you send. Model both numbers first — and the free daily cap and add-on fees on top.

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: Brevo serves a different price list depending on where you open the page, and the two are not each other's conversion: Starter and Standard differ by more than the exchange rate ($9 and $18 against €7 and €15), while Professional lands on the same 499 in both. Both ladders are below, each with the date it was read. Read on brevo.com/pricing on 6 September 2026 with the currency switched to US dollars and the yearly tab open: Free at $0 with 300 emails a day; Starter from $9 a month for 5,000 emails, or $8.08 on yearly billing; Standard from $18 ($16.17 yearly) adding marketing automation and A/B testing; Professional from $499 ($449 yearly, from 150,000 emails) with multi-user access and contact scoring; Enterprise on quote. Email volume is the headline meter, but every send tier also caps stored contacts: Free stores up to 100,000 contacts (automation on 2,000 of them); on Starter and Standard, 5,000 monthly sends store up to 500 contacts, 10,000 sends up to 1,500, 15,000 up to 2,500 and 20,000 sends or more up to 500,000; Professional stores up to 2 million and only Enterprise is unlimited (help.brevo.com, About Brevo's pricing plans, read 15 September 2026). So a big list you rarely mail still needs the send tier that stores it. Re-verified 19 September 2026 in a browser, this time in the euro view the page serves from the Netherlands and with the plan builder open: Starter €7 a month or €6.33 on yearly billing (the toggle is labelled -10%), Standard €15 or €13.50, Professional €499 or €449.08 with 10 seats included, and Free unchanged at 300 emails a day once Brevo has approved the account for sending. Two things the builder now puts on the public page that we previously had to cite the help centre for: the 5,000-email step lists 500 contacts and 1,000 web-push subscribers as included, and removing the “Sent with Brevo” footer is an €8.10-a-month add-on on Starter while Standard includes it. The Sales Essentials CRM is billed separately at €26.08 a month per seat, Sales Advanced at €53.08.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 24 October 2026 on the Free plan, in an existing Brevo account: our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We added two made-up contacts, exported them and opened the Starter checkout without paying.
findings: The account showed the Free plan with 300 emails a day ('300 / 300 Marketing & Transactional emails left') and single-user access.
A CSV file whose fields contain line breaks was misread in the import preview: the quoted line breaks became extra rows and the columns shifted. The same contacts as an XLSX file previewed correctly.
Neither the file import nor the re-import could be confirmed without ticking an opt-in agreement that our made-up addresses could not truthfully meet, so we imported no file.
We created the two contacts by hand instead. FREE_TEXT is a single-line field, so the line break could not be entered. Both contacts started as subscribed to email; we then blocklisted them.

The CSV export, downloaded through Notifications with export by email switched off, had both contacts with their external IDs, custom codes and Unicode names, plus CONTACT ID 2 and 3, but no subscription or blocklist status column.

Monthly billing was preselected. Starter (5,000 emails, 500 contacts) showed EUR 7.00 as subtotal and total due, with no VAT line; removing the Brevo logo (EUR 9.00 a month) was switched off. The plan text mentions automatic upgrades when the contact limit is reached, and the checkout box authorizing that was unticked. We stopped before paying.
not_tested: Signing up (we used an existing account)
Inviting a colleague (Free has single-user access)
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.
